chapters.title: Where it all began
chapters.blurb: Before they were Grandma and Grandpa, they were two kids from Joliet, a farm, a front porch, and a war that kept them writing letters.

chapters.title: Walter & June
chapters.blurb: A wedding on a windy June day, a honeymoon among the canyons, and a little house that would hold sixty years of life.

chapters.title: A growing family
chapters.blurb: Margaret, Robert and Eleanor arrive, and the house fills up with birthday candles, Christmas mornings and muddy shoes.

chapters.title: Summers & road trips
chapters.blurb: Every summer the station wagon got packed to the roof and pointed somewhere new, or back to the lake, which was even better.

chapters.title: Keepsakes
chapters.blurb: The things they tucked away in the cedar chest, photographed so everyone can see them up close.

chapters.title: The later years
chapters.blurb: Anniversaries, grandkids, and the long, happy porch afternoons of a life well shared.

photos.title: June, six months old
photos.caption: June in her christening gown at Kessler Studio. Grandma Rose said she wouldn't sit still until the photographer whistled 'Bye Bye Blackbird.'

photos.title: Walter and Frank on the fence
photos.caption: Walter (left) and his little brother Frank, the future Uncle Frank, on the back fence with Skip the dog. Frank always swore he was the taller one.
photos.downloadName: Walter and Frank on the fence - about 1930.jpg

photos.title: Grandma Rose on the porch
photos.caption: Grandma Rose in her rocker on the Cass Street porch, apron on as always. That geranium outlived two rocking chairs and one very determined cat.
photos.downloadName: Grandma Rose on the porch - about 1932.jpg

photos.title: The Hale farm
photos.caption: The farm outside Manhattan where Walter and Uncle Frank grew up: the red barn, the silo, and the windmill that squeaked all night long.

photos.title: Walter in uniform
photos.caption: Walter's Army portrait, taken the week before he shipped out. June kept it on her dresser through the whole war, and for most of the years after.

photos.title: V-mail from Walter
photos.caption: A V-mail letter Walter sent June from France. He mentions the rain, her mother's pies, and asks her to keep the porch light on.

photos.title: Walter & June's wedding
photos.caption: Walter and June on the steps of St. Mary's. Her veil caught the wind just as the shutter clicked, and she always said that was the best part of the wedding.

photos.title: Honeymoon at Starved Rock
photos.caption: Three days at Starved Rock for the honeymoon. Walter climbed out on the ledge for this one, and June never quite forgave him.

photos.title: Dancing at the VFW
photos.caption: Walter and June at the VFW New Year's dance. He'd been taking lessons in secret, and by then he only stepped on her feet once a night.

photos.title: Sunday picnic
photos.caption: A Sunday picnic by the water: the red checked blanket, a thermos of lemonade, and a basket June packed as if she were feeding the whole parish.
photos.downloadName: Walter and June - Sunday picnic - about 1951.jpg

photos.title: The first house
photos.caption: The day Walter and June got the keys to the little house on Hickory Street. Walter planted the maple that morning; Margaret, age two, supervised.

photos.title: June and baby Margaret
photos.caption: June with brand-new Margaret by the front window, two weeks old and already running the house.

photos.title: The first car
photos.caption: Walter's pride and joy, a two-tone Chevrolet bought used in 1955. Margaret and Robert were allowed to look at the car, not touch it.

photos.title: Robert turns three
photos.caption: Robert's third birthday party: five kids, five paper hats, three candles, and Pepper the dog waiting patiently under the table for crumbs.

photos.title: Dad on a horse at the county fair
photos.caption: Walter on a borrowed horse at the Will County Fair. He told the kids he'd been a cowboy before the war; the horse knew better.
photos.downloadName: Walter on a horse at the Will County Fair - 1957.jpg

photos.title: Sprinkler days
photos.caption: August in the backyard: Robert and Margaret racing through the sprinkler, Eleanor deciding whether to risk it, and Pepper the dog barking at all of them.

photos.title: Christmas morning
photos.caption: Christmas morning, 1961. The kids were up at five; Walter, in his good red robe, was not. That long box under the tree is the Lionel train.

photos.title: Easter on the front steps
photos.caption: Easter Sunday: Margaret in her new spring coat, Robert in a clip-on tie, and Eleanor holding the basket she wouldn't put down all day.

photos.title: The Desert Rose Motel
photos.caption: First night out on Route 66, somewhere in New Mexico. The kids voted for the motel with the pinkest neon sign, and nobody regretted it.

photos.title: The Grand Canyon
photos.caption: Walter, June, Margaret, Robert and Eleanor at the rim of the Grand Canyon. June made everyone stand well back from the railing, and then took this picture.

photos.title: The station wagon
photos.caption: The Country Squire wagon loaded to the roof, somewhere on Route 66. Walter is studying the map he never admitted he needed; Robert is "helping."

photos.title: Evening at the lake cabin
photos.caption: Evening at the cabin on Long Lake: June at the end of the dock, the rowboat tied up for the night, and supper keeping warm inside.

photos.title: Fishing with Uncle Frank
photos.caption: Uncle Frank and Robert out in the boat at dawn. Frank claimed a four-pound bass that morning; the photo, sadly, does not include the fish.

photos.title: A day at the Dunes
photos.caption: A hot July Saturday at the Indiana Dunes. June claimed the shade under the umbrella while Eleanor ran straight for Lake Michigan.
photos.downloadName: A day at the Indiana Dunes - 1971.jpg

photos.title: Campfire at the cabin
photos.caption: Last night of summer at the lake cabin: marshmallows, ghost stories from Uncle Frank, and everyone smelling like woodsmoke for a week.

photos.title: A letter to June
photos.caption: Walter's letter to June from March 1947, the spring before the wedding. Found in her jewelry box, folded and refolded until the creases went soft.

photos.title: Walter's service medal
photos.caption: Walter's World War II Victory Medal, kept in its blue box in the top dresser drawer. He never talked about it much, but he never moved it either.

photos.title: June's apple pie recipe
photos.caption: June's apple pie in her own hand, copied from Grandma Rose. The butter stain is original. Jonathan apples only, no exceptions.

photos.title: Margaret's report card
photos.caption: Margaret's fourth-grade report card: straight A's in reading, and a note from Miss Dolan about talking in class that surprised nobody in the family.

photos.title: Walter's 25-year plaque
photos.caption: The walnut plaque Joliet Steel Works gave Walter for twenty-five years of service. It hung by the back door, where he saw it every morning on his way out.
photos.downloadName: Walter Hale - 25 Years of Service plaque - 1972.jpg

photos.title: 40th anniversary party
photos.caption: Walter and June cutting the cake at their 40th anniversary party at the VFW hall. Robert gave a toast that made everyone cry, including Robert.

photos.title: Peggy and Danny in the leaves
photos.caption: Grandpa Walter raked that pile three times before Peggy and Danny let it stay a pile. Every October in the Hickory Street backyard.
photos.downloadName: Peggy and Danny in the leaves - 1991.jpg

photos.title: Grandpa's tire swing
photos.caption: Grandpa Walter giving Peggy a push on the tire swing he hung from the old maple, the same tree he planted the day he and June moved in.

photos.title: 50th anniversary
photos.caption: Fifty years. Walter and June at their golden anniversary dinner, with the balloons Danny insisted on and the corsage Walter picked out himself.

photos.title: June in her garden
photos.caption: June among her hollyhocks and roses at eighty, politely refusing all offers of help with the watering can.

photos.title: Our last Christmas together
photos.caption: Christmas 2010, the last one with Grandma June. Everyone squeezed onto the couch, and Grandpa Walter fell asleep before the pie came out.

photos.title: Walter at 95
photos.caption: Walter on the Hickory Street porch at ninety-five, cane within reach, waving at every car that went by and most of the dogs.
